reviewer.tool: agent image read tool on the captured PNGs listed below; numeric Debug HDR/channel readback, material records, environment provenance fields and the T28 Studio lighting report

observations: The lighting-probe row reads as the intended material families: white plastic/CAD, neutral gray, black leather/enamel, red paint, brass, chrome, emission and a dark blue glass sphere. Highlights are broad and soft rather than point-like, dark leather and enamel retain visible reflections, and the white patch keeps highlight headroom without clipping.
The white/gray/black reference patches stay neutral and ordered; the background remains the Windows Photos dark tone and the ground/grid are readable without washing out the dark materials.

The sphere grid shows distinct white, black, red, brass and chrome responses plus a glass sphere that transmits the grid. The brass/chrome highlights are broad and the black sphere keeps a useful reflection instead of going flat.
The glass-reference fixture reads as tinted glass: the peach and neutral spheres transmit the ground grid, keep a reflection and do not collapse into opaque alpha-blended disks.

Directional mode increases form contrast relative to Studio while preserving the same material identity and the white/gray/black ordering. Studio and Directional share the environment/BRDF path but keep their documented direct-light difference.
The STL box is neutral, evenly lit and reads as CAD rather than a scan; the soft contact footprint and grid keep the object grounded without a heavy shadow.
Car: the red paint, windshield reflection and dark interior are readable from the front and oblique views; the glass is not a flat overlay and the paint does not clip.

Camera: the black body keeps edge and top highlights, the lens ring/depth is visible, and the dark body remains distinguishable from the backdrop. It retains the reflection/depth behaviour the earlier reviews required.
Suit: the orange fabric, gray helmet and blue cuffs/gloves read as separate materials with no ghosting, opacity workaround or whole-model brightening.
No per-model-name or per-material-name exception is present in the renderer or the lane; the presentation choice follows contributed surface shares and the catalog profile.

defects.label: limitation
defects.where: procedural Studio environment, visible on lighting-probe, sphere-grid, Car and Camera
defects.description: The product-owned procedural bake still mixes warm/cool panel separations rather than matching a measured third-party studio HDRI. T28 calibrates the shipped bake and records the neutral reference comparison; it does not ship an external HDR.

defects.label: limitation
defects.description: The shipping environment remains a product-owned procedural bake. The neutral reference exists only for the measured T28 comparison and is never selected automatically; a licensed external HDR bake remains future work rather than a hidden asset dependency.

positives: The camera-relative key/fill/rim rig and the world-stable IBL are explicitly separated: the CPU owns the base intensities and the shader has no second undocumented intensity source.
Environment intensity scales the direct rig and IBL together, preserving the F3D-style intensity relationship and the existing exposure/background preferences.
The automatic preset decision uses contributed triangle shares, so a small glass detail cannot force the transparency checker and density alone cannot turn an authored PBR mesh into a scan.
Environment provenance (version 2, product variant, identity hash, resident bytes and bake time) is exposed read-only for evidence and stays bounded.

The generated material matrix, glass fixture and Car/Camera/Suit external views all render without a per-asset exception; review evidence is separated from ordinary verification and no reference was promoted.

acceptance.acceptedReferencesPromotedBy: not applicable for T28 (observed evidence only)
